claim: 71/384 factorial runs were slowed by a co-tenant process on GPU 0 (median 0.60x of true throughput).
caveat: The other process is inferred from device memory and clocks; its owner was not observed during the run.

claim: Repetitions of contaminated cells agreed to within 0.2-3.8% (CV), so within-session noise does not reveal this kind of interference.
With the original accuracy policy, spec + prefix is the best configuration at 6 of 7 workloads.
Corrected best speedups (policy A): centre 1.82x, short prompts 1.93x, long prompts 1.50x, low concurrency 2.48x, high concurrency 1.67x, 0% reuse 1.39x, 90% reuse 2.62x
caveat: 16 contaminated cells could not be re-run; a missing cell could be a better configuration.

claim: No combination with measured singles fell >5% below the product of its single speedups; 18 of 50 exceeded it by >5%, all involving spec.
caveat: Only points where all five singles were measured (centre, high concurrency, 0%/90% reuse).

claim: Multiplicative composition predicts centre combinations with median error 4.8%; additive composition 9.1%.
spec x prefix interaction rises from 1.01 (0% reuse) to 1.12 (50%) and 1.22 (90%).
The spec x prefix synergy is explained by Amdahl's law over mixed prefill/decode engine steps.
caveat: Consistent with the measured decode-time reductions; not proven by a controlled ablation.

claim: FP8 weights give 1.20x alone and 1.34x on top of EAGLE-3 at the centre.
quant x spec synergy arises because spec makes steps compute-heavier, where FP8 math helps most.
caveat: Supported by tokens per step; kernel-level confirmation would need per-kernel profiles of both configs.

claim: EAGLE-3 speedup falls from 1.35x (2048-token prompts) to 1.00x (6144).
caveat: Synthetic random-word prompts; real long documents may behave differently.

claim: The EAGLE-3 head was trained on shorter contexts than 4k tokens.
caveat: Inferred from the acceptance pattern; the head's training length was not checked.

claim: FP8 weights + FP8 KV lose 2.6 points on GSM8K (p = 0.03); each alone is not significant.
caveat: Single run per setting (greedy decoding); quant+spec and kvq+spec were not paired-tested.

claim: Tuned batching has no effect at any workload (limit never binds).
spec's main effect ranges from 1.00x to 2.31x by workload.
GPU busy 96%-99% in all profiler traces; power-cap throttle in all runs.
caveat: Profiles cover 64 engine steps per configuration.

claim: Running cells concurrently on the two GPUs does not change their throughput.
